pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/components/dashboard/spa/scopeHonesty.test.ts:64 The structural pin searches for the bare identifier "CompareToggle" in the scope bar's source, so a comment naming the old toggle (any prose that spells it) turns the suite red. That is the over-match direction pin-the-call-not-the-name names: the needle has no token that only code could produce.

techniques.evidence: src/components/dashboard/spa/scopeHonesty.test.ts:64 Absence pin on a bare identifier that prose can spell. Line 39's needle "useDashboardScope()" has an empty argument list, which a comment can also spell. Line 59 shows the right shape: a needle with an argument list.

src/components/dashboard/spa/scopeHonesty.test.ts:40 The scope filter is lifted into a reachable unit (scopeProjections, tested on the fixtures), and each call site's adoption is asserted as well, which is what the shared-predicate rule asks for.

src/components/dashboard/spa/scopeHonesty.test.ts:34 The walk's population comes from viewTraits and is checked against the pinned table in both directions, so a view that gains the scope bar with no data module goes red instead of passing as an empty selection.

src/components/dashboard/scope/scopeProjections.test.ts:55 The demo world is folded once per file into read-only constants that every case reads. The 'going back' case (line 172) shows that no hidden state carries between calls.

pairs.registryProposal: pin-the-call-not-the-name's decision rules talk about ordering claims and presence needles. They could state the ABSENCE case outright: a not.toContain over a bare identifier is the over-match direction in its plainest form, because any comment naming the removed construct fails the pin.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/reviews/reviews-split-pane/ReviewList.tsx:64 The repeated review row's test identifier is the bare role with no entity id, even though review.id is on the same line. The production-build Playwright spec has to re-find a row by its displayed aria-label (e2e/review-undo.spec.ts:45), so the lookup breaks if a label changes or two reviews share one.

techniques.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/reviews/reviews-split-pane/ReviewList.tsx:64 The test-identifier contract says a repeated element's identifier combines its role with the entity's stable id. Here the role stands alone. The product's own keyboard navigation also queries this attribute (ReviewsSplitPane.tsx:102), so it is not used only by the harness.
